question: Should OpenClaw sponsor the experimental core Claws lifecycle stack, including this Doctor diagnostics slice, for sequential landing after its ownership prerequisites?
rationale: The implementation is intentionally gated and well-evidenced, but whether lifecycle ownership and diagnostics belong in core is a product and architecture commitment that cannot be resolved by patch correctness alone.

options.title: Sponsor staged landing
options.body: Approve the experimental core direction, require the documentation gate correction, then land this PR only after its prerequisite ownership slice is merged or safely rebased.

options.title: Defer the core experiment
options.body: Keep the PR open but pause stack landing until maintainers decide whether Claw lifecycle ownership should remain a core responsibility.

options.title: Redirect the feature boundary
options.body: Decline the core lifecycle direction and ask for a narrower plugin or external package proposal if an adequate extension seam can support it.

recommendation.title: Sponsor staged landing
recommendation.body: Approve the experimental core direction, require the documentation gate correction, then land this PR only after its prerequisite ownership slice is merged or safely rebased.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen is assigned to the PR and authored the current integration commit, making them the clearest available routing point for the stack decision.
